basis: Retinal dystrophy, obesity and digital anomalies are core features; developmental delay 2/2, intellectual disability 2/4. Renal insufficiency 1/3 omitted at cap.

decisions.renal: none: renal insufficiency in 1/3 qualifies, but is omitted at the four-axis cap in favor of more frequent defining manifestations.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: polydactyly is a major BBS criterion; brachydactyly and syndactyly each occur in 2/2 reported patients.

basis: Neuronopathic storage disorder; skeletal/joint disease >80% and obstructive airway disease >70%. Common valvular disease (>50%) and hearing loss omitted at cap.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: valvular storage disease affects >50%, but is omitted at the cap in favor of very frequent skeletal disease and severe airway involvement.
decisions.pulmonary: involved: airway glycosaminoglycan deposition and structural airway dysfunction affect >70%; direct obstruction contributes substantially to mortality.

basis: Autoimmune autonomic ganglion injury; gastrointestinal, bladder and circulatory dysfunction reflects neural failure rather than direct injury to those organs.

decisions.renal: none: bladder dysfunction is common (~50%), but results from autonomic denervation without established direct urinary-organ injury.
decisions.gastrointestinal: none: dysmotility is common (~70-80%), but reflects autonomic neural injury rather than direct gastrointestinal tissue damage.

basis: Severe skeletal dysplasia; pulmonary hypoplasia and structural airway disease cause direct respiratory impairment in >30% across the group.

decisions.pulmonary: involved: pulmonary hypoplasia and laryngotracheobronchomalacia commonly cause respiratory failure (>30% across types), beyond thoracic restriction alone.

basis: GPI biosynthesis disorder; delayed myelination/severe developmental delay and ankle contracture each reported in 1/1. Hair texture/sparsity alone lacks clear functional injury.

decisions.dermatologic: none: sparse/coarse hair in 1/1 is reported, but does not establish damaging cutaneous involvement.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: ankle flexion contracture in 1/1 is persistent locomotor impairment; the frequency estimate is limited by the single reported patient.

basis: SCID with defining exfoliative dermatitis, alopecia and inflammatory enteropathy; hepatomegaly alone does not establish functionally damaging hepatic infiltration.

decisions.hepatic: none: hepatomegaly is common (>30%), but damaging hepatic infiltration or liver dysfunction at that frequency is not established.

basis: Pathological blood coagulation forms thrombi in vessels or heart chambers; both coagulation and vascular axes define the disease. Downstream organ damage varies by site.

decisions.haematologic: primary: pathological clot formation is a disorder of blood coagulation, regardless of whether the trigger is endothelial injury or a systemic coagulation defect.

basis: Cervical vertebral fusion; hearing impairment is 30-79% by HPO, and renal/urinary malformations affect ~30%. Individual renal anomaly types can each be below 30%.

decisions.renal: involved: renal/urinary malformations collectively affect ~30%; frequent genitourinary HPO supports this despite each individual renal anomaly being occasional.

basis: Storage disorder with defining neurodegeneration and ichthyosis; visual impairment 80-99%. Skeletal and hearing disease (30-79%) omitted at cap; organomegaly alone insufficient.

decisions.neurologic: primary: progressive neurologic deterioration and developmental impairment are defining manifestations, present in 80-99%.
decisions.dermatologic: primary: ichthyosis is a defining manifestation in 80-99%, supported by the integumentary-system parent.

basis: Localized chronic inflammatory dermatosis with immune-mediated cutaneous small-vessel vasculitis; vascular involvement qualifies even when confined to skin.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: cutaneous small-vessel vasculitis is part of the lesion itself; the cardiovascular axis includes vessels regardless of their location.
